newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-QBE says not interested in buying bank.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-QBE says not interested in buying bank.

text.p: QBE Insurance Group Ltd managing director John Cloney said on Tuesday the group would not be interested in buying any bank after the completion of the Wallis inquiry into financial regulation.

"QBE ought to be allowed to buy a bank if it wishes to do so but it is my own personal view and, I believe the view of the board, that we will not be doing that," Cloney told reporters after the company's annual meeting.
The Wallis inquiry is widely expected in the financial community to free up merger rules for financial institutions.

Cloney said QBE continued to watch out for acquisition opportunities and that QBE had about A$400 million available for such acquisitions. "We are on the lookout all the time, and there are a couple of things that may come to pass," Cloney said, adding however that he could not be more specific.
He said any acquisition would have to pass high hurdle rates of return to ensure QBE's currently strong earnings growth was not diluted.
Cloney referred to the returns already evident from its September purchase for A$70 million of Britain's Allstate Insurance group.
"That will give us in excess of 15 percent return (on equity invested) in this fiscal year," he said.
"They're the sort of hurdle rates we set," he said.

"Because we're already earning 17 percent (return on shareholders funds) we're not in the position to spend up large and say we'll get a pay back in three or four years, because it will dilute our overall earnings," he said.
Cloney said Australian acquisitions were less likely because the current targets were unlikely to achieves such high returns quickly.

"So far as Australia is concerned, to acquire at the sort of hurdle rates of return we're looking for is a little difficult because I think there are more people interested in what's available here than overseas," Cloney said.
